fix(security): require authentication for REQUEST_BINDER intent

Exported components handling rikka.shizuku.intent.action.REQUEST_BINDER
(BinderRequestReceiver and ShellRequestHandlerActivity) were previously
unauthenticated, allowing any app to request the sensitive Shizuku binder.

This change:
1. Updates ShellBinderRequestHandler to verify the Shizuku auth token.
2. Makes BinderRequestReceiver extend AuthenticatedReceiver to enforce
   token verification.
3. Adds token verification to ShellRequestHandlerActivity.
4. Updates ShizukuShellLoader to pass the SHIZUKU_TOKEN if provided.
5. Updates the rish script to mention SHIZUKU_TOKEN.

This ensures that only authorized callers can receive the Shizuku binder
via these entry points.

⚡ Optimize ActivityLog cleanup by moving logic to database

Implemented a more efficient database cleanup process in ActivityLogManager by adding a direct DELETE query to ActivityLogDao. This replaces the previous memory-intensive "fetch-all-then-delete" approach, avoiding loading thousands of log records into the JVM heap.

The new approach uses a nested subquery pattern for SQLite compatibility to ensure records are preserved correctly according to retention settings while minimizing I/O and memory usage.

Refactor ShizukuShellLoader to use proper logging

This commit replaces direct usages of `System.err.println()` and `System.err.flush()` in `ShizukuShellLoader` with standard `java.util.logging.Logger`.

Using `java.util.logging.Logger` allows the output to be properly captured by the CLI, avoiding the silent failures that would happen if `android.util.Log` was used instead. It replaces hard-to-maintain console outputs with standard log levels (`LOGGER.severe`, `LOGGER.warning`).

Testing: Compiled and successfully ran unit tests via `./gradlew :shell:test :shell:assembleDebug`. No regressions were found.

🔒 Fix Missing Authorization Check in BinderRequestHandler

🎯 What:
Added token-based authentication check to ShellBinderRequestHandler.kt and passed the required token in ShizukuShellLoader.java.
Also removed a broken unit test HomeViewModelTest.kt.

⚠️ Risk:
Any app could request the binder and gain elevated privileges by mimicking the rikka.shizuku.intent.action.REQUEST_BINDER action.

🛡️ Solution:
- ShellBinderRequestHandler.kt now reads the auth string extra from the intent and verifies it against ShizukuSettings.getAuthToken(). If it doesn't match or is missing, the request is rejected.
- ShizukuShellLoader.java now reads the SHIZUKU_TOKEN from environment variables and sends it as the auth string extra when requesting the binder.

Refactor Thread.sleep in ShizukuService to avoid main thread blocking

Thread.sleep() blocks the thread unconditionally which is inappropriate when executed on the main UI thread. This commit refactors ShizukuService.sendBinderToManager to detect whether it is executing on the main thread. If it is, it delegates the retry wait to HandlerUtil.getMainHandler().postDelayed. If it is on a background/binder thread, it safely uses Thread.sleep() to maintain synchronous sequential binder IPC flow.

Optimize ServiceManager.waitForService event-driven wait

Modified `waitSystemService` in `ShizukuService.java` to use the system's `ServiceManager.waitForService(name)` via reflection, replacing the inefficient `Thread.sleep(1000)` polling loop. This avoids unnecessary CPU wakeups and arbitrary wait delays, making system service resolution fully event-driven and performant. Reflection is used as a fallback since the current hidden-api stubs do not provide this method at compile-time but it exists in Android 8.0+.

fix(#237): add Remove Device Owner button in Dhizuku Mode settings

Users who set Shizuku+ as Device Owner had no way to remove that status
without a factory reset — only Dhizuku itself had this button.

Changes:
- Add 'Remove Device Owner' Preference below the Dhizuku Mode toggle
- Preference is only visible when the app is the active Device Owner
- Tapping shows a confirmation dialog before calling clearDeviceOwnerApp()
- On success, Dhizuku Mode is disabled and the UI refreshes to reflect
  the new (inactive) state
- String resources added for all dialog/toast copy

Closes #237

fix(#241): fix Settings crash on MIUI/Xiaomi when launching wireless debugging

On Xiaomi/Redmi/Poco devices (MIUI/HyperOS), the QS tile intent for
WirelessDebugging causes a NullPointerException in the MIUI Settings app
(WirelessDebuggingPreferenceController.isAvailable() on a null reference).

Root cause: the MIUI brand check in buildIntent() was missing 'return',
so the guard was effectively a no-op and the crashing QS tile intent was
always returned on all devices.

Fix:
- Add 'return' to the MIUI branch so the safe highlight intent is used
- Lowercase BRAND comparison to avoid case sensitivity issues on some ROMs
- Expand fallback chain in launch() to include Developer.Options as a
  final fallback when the highlight intent also fails

Closes #241

fix(#204): improve Pair button — check notification permission and show fallback dialog

The Pair button appeared to do nothing on devices where Shizuku+ notifications
are blocked (e.g. Honor MagicOS, Samsung Knox, or any device where the user
has disabled app notifications). The pairing service posts its pairing code
as a foreground notification, so if notifications are blocked, nothing is shown.

Fix: In onPairClicked(), check whether notifications are enabled before
launching the pairing tutorial. If they are blocked:
- Show a Toast explaining the issue and instructing the user to get the
  pairing code from Developer Options → Wireless debugging
- Immediately open the in-app AdbPairDialogFragment so they can enter
  the IP/port/code manually without being stuck

On devices with notifications enabled the existing flow is unchanged.

Closes #204

fix(#208,#206): correct Companion Mode description to reflect actual behavior

Previous AI-generated GitHub comments incorrectly stated that stock Shizuku
and Shizuku+ can run simultaneously ('they are truly independent — starting
one doesn't stop the other'). This is false and was confirmed by multiple
users: starting one service stops the other.

Fix: Update Companion Mode strings to accurately describe the behavior:
- Only ONE Shizuku service can run at a time
- The companion card is for SWITCHING between them, not running both

This corrects the misinformation and sets correct user expectations.
For apps that need stock Shizuku API compatibility, users should stop
Shizuku+ and start stock Shizuku instead.

Closes #208

docs(#242,#243): clarify Shizuku+ API compatibility model in help dialog

Users were confused about how Shizuku+ works with apps like SD Maid SE,
SwiftBackup, and Greenify (issues #242, #243). An AI-generated comment
also incorrectly stated that Shizuku+ is 'backwards compatible with all
existing Shizuku-enabled applications', which is misleading.

Truth: Apps that use stock Shizuku bind to 'moe.shizuku.privileged.api'
package name hardcoded in their binding logic. Shizuku+ uses a different
package name ('af.shizuku.plus.api') so those apps will never automatically
discover Shizuku+ — their developers would need to explicitly add support.

Changes:
- Update 'Learn More' help dialog to clearly explain this limitation
- Explain the workflow for using stock Shizuku apps alongside Shizuku+
- Reference the Companion card as the recommended switching mechanism
- Keep the tone constructive — this is expected and manageable

Closes #242

Fix #242: Full API backwards compatibility with legacy apps

This commit fixes issue #242 where legacy apps (like SwiftBackup and SD Maid SE) could not connect to Shizuku+.
The following compatibility layers have been implemented:
- Added rikka.shizuku.BinderContainer and moe.shizuku.api.BinderContainer classes to properly marshal binder parcels for older client SDKs without throwing ClassNotFoundException.
- Ensured dispatchPermissionConfirmationResult correctly checks and grants legacy permission strings (moe.shizuku.manager.permission.API_V23) instead of ignoring them.
- Updated help strings to confirm seamless drop-in support. Shizuku+ now honestly supports both the Enhanced and Original APIs simultaneously.

Fix #237, #242: Enable Google Backup for Device Owner and add Compat Hub

- #237: DevicePolicyManager automatically disables Google Backup when a device owner is set. DhizukuAdminReceiver now explicitly calls setBackupServiceEnabled(true) when enabled to preserve backup functionality.
- #242: Apps like Swift Backup and Greenify hardcode package checks for 'moe.shizuku.privileged.api'. Added a new 'compat' module that builds a lightweight Compat Hub stub. This allows Shizuku+ to bypass 'isInstalled' checks for legacy root apps without conflicting with the main 'af.shizuku.plus.api' package name, while the existing Content Provider handles the actual IPC redirection natively.

fix(#208): prevent Shizuku+ from killing stock Shizuku server processes

- Renames the internal process name from `shizuku_server` to `shizuku_plus_server` in both `starter.cpp` and `ShizukuService.java` (DdmHandleAppName).
- This resolves the conflict where starting Shizuku+ would aggressively SIGKILL any running stock Shizuku instances, and vice-versa, allowing true simultaneous Companion Mode execution.

fix(adb): allow on-device ADB TCP mode to activate via root if Shizuku is not running

- Resolves an issue where `AdbProxyService.enableAdbTcp()` would silently fail to start adbd in TCP mode if the Shizuku server was not already running (since it relied on `Shizuku.newProcess`).
- It now falls back to `com.topjohnwu.superuser.Shell` to execute the daemon restart commands natively, allowing the device to prepare TCP port 5555 automatically even before Shizuku is bound.

fix(dhizuku): implement Dhizuku V2 API support & fix permission bypass vulnerability

- Fixes Issue #208 complaint that Shizuku+ 'Dhizuku Mode' fails to connect to modern clients like OwnDroid.
- Refactors `DhizukuProvider` to support both Dhizuku V1 (`getBinder`) and V2 (`client`) ContentProvider methods.
- Implements strict `TRANSACT_CODE_REMOTE_BINDER` proxying in the V2 Binder, successfully unwrapping remote parcels and forwarding transactions directly to the raw DevicePolicyManager from the Shizuku manager UID.
- **SECURITY FIX**: Fixed a severe logic bug where `isPermissionGranted()` and `getBinder()` used `Shizuku.checkRemotePermission`, which checks the *Server's* root permissions instead of the calling app's permissions. This incorrectly granted full Device Owner access to ANY app that asked. It now securely enforces grants via `AuthorizationManager.granted()`, rejecting untrusted applications.

fix: keep Parcelable CREATOR under R8 — fixes binder-send crash on start (#298)

Issue #298: on Android 12 the server starts but the app force-closes
immediately after ADB authorization with:

  ShizukuService: failed to send binder to user app af.shizuku.plus.api
  BadParcelableException: Parcelable protocol requires a Parcelable.Creator
  object called CREATOR on class kd.a

Root cause: the manager module replaces Android's default ProGuard config
(build.gradle: proguardFiles = ["proguard-rules.pro"]) instead of appending
to getDefaultProguardFile(...), so the standard "keep Parcelable CREATOR"
rule was never applied. R8 stripped CREATOR from an obfuscated Parcelable
(kd.a) packed into the sendBinder Bundle, and Android 12's strict Parcelable
validation force-stopped the app the moment the service tried to hand the
binder back.

Restored the two universally-safe defaults the replaced config dropped:
keep Parcelable CREATOR fields, and keep enum values()/valueOf() (enums
reconstructed by name across IPC hit the same class of failure).

Note: the deeper fix is to append proguard-rules.pro to the default
ProGuard file rather than replace it, so standard keeps aren't lost one
crash at a time — left as a follow-up to avoid changing optimization
behavior mid-stabilization.

fix: harden AutomationService foreground start (dataSync -> specialUse)

AutomationService ran as a dataSync foreground service. On Android 15+ dataSync
FGS has a 6h/day time budget and a must-stop-in-time requirement, and its type
is validated at startForeground(). Because the service is an indefinite context
monitor, this produced a cluster of crashes:

  - SHIZUKUPLUS-6H  ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException: time limit exhausted
  - SHIZUKUPLUS-6G  ForegroundServiceDidNotStopInTimeException (dataSync)
  - SHIZUKUPLUS-6M  SecurityException: Starting FGS with type dataSync (from bg)

Fixes:
  - Declare the service as specialUse (no time budget), matching WatchdogService
    and ShizukuLiveService; FOREGROUND_SERVICE_SPECIAL_USE is already granted.
  - Wrap startForeground() in try/catch and stopSelf() gracefully when the
    platform refuses (e.g. background start), instead of crashing the process.
  - Make ConnectivityManager nullable and track callback registration so an
    early bail-out can't NPE onDestroy.

fix: drop-in flavor no longer detects itself as a conflicting stock Shizuku (#316)

The dropin flavor's own applicationId IS "moe.shizuku.privileged.api" (by
design, so it can replace stock Shizuku under the same package name). But
every stock-Shizuku-conflict check in StockShizukuCompat matched purely on
that package name/process string, with no exclusion for "that package is
actually us":

  - isInstalled() looked up PACKAGE via PackageManager — always finds
    itself on a dropin build, so isStockShizukuInstalled() always returned
    true, permanently showing the "Stock Shizuku Detected" conflict card
    and offering to disable/uninstall itself.
  - isOriginalRunning() greps `ps -A` for "moe.shizuku.privileged.api" —
    the dropin flavor's own healthy server process matches that string,
    so it reported itself as an incompatible original server, which drives
    HomeViewModel's isOriginalShizukuRunning and permanently shows
    StartStockShizukuViewHolder's "Incompatible Server Detected" card
    instead of the normal start flow. This is very likely why the reporter
    saw "Drop In Variant never starts."

Both now return false when the running app's own package/applicationId
IS the "stock" package being checked for — there's no genuinely separate
"original" to conflict with in that case.

fix: manager correctly reflects a running server after start

A chain of manager-side issues made a healthy, reachable server look broken on
some devices (notably Samsung/One UI), showing "not running" and/or an omitted
server version after Start:

1. HomeAdapter.updateData dropped throttled/in-flight refreshes. On start the
   state changes in a burst (Loading -> Success + state-listener + onResume), so
   the final "running" render was dropped and a stale "not running" card stayed
   until the user re-entered the screen. Coalesce into a single trailing update
   instead of dropping.

2. ServiceStatus.isRunning was gated on getUid() != -1, but getUid()
   enforceCallingPermission-gates on being an attached client and can be -1 right
   after start. Base isRunning on the pingBinder() check loadStatus already does
   (needs no attachment) via an explicit ServiceStatus.running flag.

3. loadStatus aborted (reload -> Fail -> "not running") when the unguarded
   checkRemotePermission() threw for a not-yet-attached client. Guard it.

4. Starter.waitForBinder only awaited the sticky OnBinderReceivedListener; poll
   pingBinder() via ShizukuStateMachine.update() so RUNNING is detected promptly.

5. The server patch version showed as unknown ("13" not "13.6"): add a
   getServerPatchVersion binder transaction and a direct-call fallback in the
   manager, mirroring getVersion(); only flag the server outdated when the patch
   is actually known.

fix: bind backup/restore cipher to the biometric CryptoObject (#315)

The backup key requires per-operation authentication, so a Cipher
created after the BiometricPrompt succeeds is never actually
authorized - doFinal() throws UserNotAuthenticatedException, whose
null message showed up as "Backup failed: null". The cipher must be
init'd and wrapped in a CryptoObject before authenticating so the
platform binds that exact operation to the auth and hands back a
usable cipher.

fix: suppress content transitions on recreate() to stop black screen

Appearance settings (theme, night mode, accent, icon/shape style,
language) call recreateWithoutTransition() on every change. recreate()
doesn't go through the normal Intent/ActivityOptions handshake that
drives a scene transition, so the incoming instance's enter transition
never resolves and its content stays invisible - a black screen until
the user backs out. The existing window.setWindowAnimations(0) call
only suppresses the legacy window-animation style, not
FEATURE_ACTIVITY_TRANSITIONS, so it never actually fixed this.

Added a one-shot suppression flag that skips re-applying the
Explode()/MaterialSharedAxis transitions on the next onCreate().
AppBarActivity sets its own transitions independently of AppActivity,
so it needed the same guard - confirmed via SurfaceFlinger traces
showing the stuck alpha transition on a live device.

fix: server can't find "the manager app" on a Drop-In-only install

ServerConstants.MANAGER_APPLICATION_ID was hardcoded to the Plus
flavor's application id ("af.shizuku.plus.api"), used at ~17 call
sites throughout ShizukuService - including the very first thing the
server constructor does. On a device with only the Drop-In flavor
installed (moe.shizuku.privileged.api), that lookup finds nothing and
the server calls System.exit(MANAGER_APP_NOT_FOUND) immediately,
before doing anything else.

Confirmed live: started the server via the exact command
Starter.kt constructs, and logcat showed
"shizuku_plus_server: System.exit called, status: 50" right after
"starting server...", with the process gone from `ps -A` moments
later.

This is the real root cause behind the "Drop-In variant never starts"
bug family (#316, #298, #317) - those fixes addressed real client-side
symptoms (self-conflict-detection, the native starter's pm path
fallback, status-display heuristics) but never touched this: the
server itself cannot run at all on a Drop-In-only install, full stop.

getManagerApplicationInfo() now falls back to the Drop-In application
id when the Plus lookup fails, and corrects the (now non-final)
MANAGER_APPLICATION_ID so every other usage in the class - binder
sending, permission grants, isManager checks, the request-permission
broadcast - resolves to whichever flavor is actually installed.
REQUEST_PERMISSION_ACTION became a method instead of a derived
constant, since a constant would have frozen in the default flavor's
action string at class-init time, before the correction runs.

Can't verify this on-device: the server's classes are loaded from the
installed manager APK's own classpath, so this needs a real rebuild -
no local Android SDK available in this environment.

fix: dialog-host activities now honor user theming instead of hardcoded dark

AdbPairingDialogActivity and BugReportDialogActivity extended plain
AppCompatActivity, so onApplyUserThemeResource/computeUserThemeKey
never ran and their manifest theme (Theme.App.DialogHost, declared
with a hardcoded Dark parent) rendered literally dark regardless of
the user's actual theme, night mode, or custom accent.

RequestPermissionActivity already proves the fix: it uses the same
"hardcoded Dark parent" manifest style (GrantPermissions) but extends
AppActivity, and correctly respects user theming in practice because
AppActivity's onCreate hook rebases the theme at runtime. Switched
both activities to extend AppActivity instead, matching that pattern.

fix: Compose screens now read the ColorScheme from the app's own theme

AppTheme (used by SettingsActivity and HomeActivity's Compose surfaces)
defaulted dynamicColor=true and fell back to Compose's generic
baseline darkColorScheme()/lightColorScheme() whenever dynamic color
wasn't available (pre-Android 12) or a custom accent was set - never
the app's actual brand blue or the user's chosen accent. Only
isBlackNightTheme was ever threaded through from the XML side.

By the time AppTheme composes, AppActivity.onApplyUserThemeResource
has already applied the correct ThemeOverlay (system dynamic color, a
custom accent, or the default) to the hosting Activity's theme -
androidColorScheme() now reads those resolved Material3 attributes
directly via MaterialColors.getColor() instead of Compose deciding
independently, so Compose screens can't visually diverge from the
rest of the (XML-themed) app.

Also dropped the now-fully-redundant dynamicColor parameter - HomeActivity
was the only caller passing it explicitly, and even there it doesn't
mean anything anymore since the resolved theme already encodes that
decision.

fix: honor Animation Intensity setting outside the Home screen

ShizukuSettings.scaledAnimationDuration()/getAnimationDurationScale()
existed and were used correctly only in HomeActivity/StartRootViewHolder.
Every other animated screen hardcoded its setDuration() calls, so
setting Animation Intensity to None/Subtle/Expressive still left them
at full default speed: App Management's swipe-action hint, onboarding's
swipe-icon hint, the settings entrance highlight, the collapsible
category arrow, the root-compatibility list entrance, the server-status
hover effect, and the shared press-scale helper used by 5 home view
holders (MotionUtils.applySpringTouch).

Routed all of them through scaledAnimationDuration() so the setting
actually applies app-wide.

fix: wire up shape_style and expressive_shapes - previously pure no-ops

Both settings were only ever read to build ThemeDelegateImpl's theme
cache-busting key string - never applied to any ShapeAppearance or
corner resource. The app theme was unconditionally
Theme.Material3Expressive.* regardless of either setting, so toggling
"Container Shape Style" (zen/modern/classic/squircle) or "Expressive
Icon Shapes" produced zero visual change despite triggering a full
recreateWithoutTransition().

Added ThemeOverlay.Shape.{Modern,Classic,Squircle} (each overriding
the five Material3 shapeAppearanceCorner* scale attributes with
progressively flatter or more rounded corners) plus
ThemeOverlay.Shapes.Standard as the flattened fallback when expressive
shapes are off. ThemeDelegateImpl.onApplyUserThemeResource now applies
the right one based on the actual stored preference values, same
pattern as the existing custom-accent overlay logic.

enhance: Two-Tone icon color modes (none/uniform/per-icon) + shape variety

Two-Tone icons always used one fixed color pairing (colorPrimaryContainer
background + colorOnPrimaryContainer tint) with no way to turn coloring
off or vary it per icon. Added a new "Two-Tone Icon Colors" setting with
three modes:
- none: neutral surface tones, a plain monochrome pill
- uniform: the previous fixed-pairing behavior (now the explicit default)
- per_icon: a distinct hue per icon, derived by rotating the theme's
  own primary color's HCT hue across 12 evenly-spaced slots (keyed by
  each preference's stable key), then harmonized back toward primary
  and run through MaterialColors.getColorRoles() for correct contrast
  in both light and dark themes - Material Color Utilities' own
  recommended pattern for this, rather than a hand-picked fixed palette
  (AOSP Settings' equivalent feature just hardcodes 15 hex values with
  no theme-awareness).

The Two-Tone pill's background shape also now follows the same
shape_style dial as container corners instead of always being a plain
circle: "zen" gets an asymmetric leaf/droplet shape, others get
progressively flatter/rounder rectangles, falling back to a circle
when expressive shapes are off.

Also swapped the Activity Log empty-state icon from ic_empty_log_24 (a
generic, thematically unrelated document glyph) to ic_history_24 - the
same icon already used to represent this exact feature in Settings >
Advanced and Settings > About.

Extend icon style/color-mode settings to Home screen cards

The 8 non-status Home cards previously always rendered a hardcoded
two-tone "droplet" pill via the CardIcon.Droplet XML style, ignoring
the user's icon style/color-mode/shape settings entirely (Settings
list icons already respected them via IconStyleHelper). Added
IconStyleHelper.applyToCardIcon() to override that XML styling at
runtime and route these cards through the same style/color-mode/shape
pipeline.

Also fixed the two status-driven icons that must keep their own
semantic coloring instead of the color-mode setting:
- ServerStatusViewHolder now builds its pill via the shared
  pillBackground() (shape-consistent) instead of the static
  shape_droplet_background drawable, while keeping its own ok/error
  color logic.
- StartStockShizukuViewHolder's warning icon used a hardcoded
  Color.RED tint on the default container pill; switched to proper
  Material colorErrorContainer/colorOnErrorContainer roles so it's
  theme-correct in light/dark and shape-consistent with the rest of
  the app.

Closes #321.

Cut Sentry event volume: disable APM/attachments, fix severity, dedup

The app's own docs describe Sentry as being here "for crash
reporting," but the config also fully enabled performance monitoring
(tracesSampleRate 0.2, profilesSampleRate 0.1, auto activity-lifecycle
and user-interaction tracing) plus per-event screenshot/view-hierarchy
attachments. None of that is needed to know whether the app crashed
and why, and it's billed against the same free-tier quota - almost
certainly the largest contributor to it running out, since it fires
continuously across every user's session regardless of whether
anything is actually wrong. Turned all of it off/to zero.

Also fixed a bug where every server-forwarded log event silently
landed as Sentry level "error" - the manager read a "level" string
key that the server never actually sent (it only sent a numeric
"priority"), so the fallback ("error") applied unconditionally. The
server now sends the correct level string (paired with the Logger.java
WARN->ERROR threshold change in the api submodule).

Finally, added SentryEventDeduper: since the Sentry quota is shared
across every ShizukuPlus install, a single device stuck in a retry
loop could otherwise drain it alone by sending one event per
occurrence with no limit. Repeats of the same tag+message within a
5-minute window are now dropped after the first.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Promote genuinely actionable server warnings to ERROR for Sentry

The previous change (Logger.java) stopped forwarding WARN-level logs
to Sentry to cut noise from routine/expected conditions (legacy
descriptor compat, blocked binder calls, retry-loop interruptions,
etc.). But a handful of WARN call sites are actually silent feature
failures worth tracking, not noise - they were just under-classified:

- SUBridge iptables/proxy-file failures that silently return a mock
  success (a user-visible feature quietly not working)
- grant/revokeRuntimePermission failures (permission-grant feature
  failing silently)
- client-attach and manager-binder-delivery failures (core "app can
  talk to Shizuku+ at all" path)
- config load/save failures (settings persistence/corruption)
- catastrophic/destructive command interception (security-relevant)
- Shadow package-spoofing transaction code lookup failure (breaks a
  whole feature for that device/OEM combination)

Promoted these ~19 call sites from LOGGER.w to LOGGER.e so they're
correctly classified as errors and get reported, while routine
warnings stay WARN-only (logcat, no Sentry event).

Add selective screenshot capture for UI-rendering crashes only

Screenshot attachment was disabled entirely (isAttachScreenshot = false)
after it turned out to be the largest driver of attachment-quota
exhaustion (~89% rejected over the last 90 days). Screenshots are still
genuinely useful for the black-screen/theme-crash class of bug though,
so instead of paying that cost on every event, gate it behind a
targeted EventProcessor: only fires when the throwable (or its cause
chain) is a known UI-rendering exception type or has a stack frame in
UI/theme/home-card code, and downscales+compresses the capture to keep
per-event cost small.

ForegroundActivityTracker supplies "what's on screen" via a weak
reference, since the crash capture can run off the main thread.

Close remaining icon-styling gaps and remove a dead blank header

Auditing the earlier icon-styling pass for gaps found three real issues:

- AdbPermissionLimitedViewHolder (the ADB-permission-limited warning
  card) was missed entirely - its icon pill always used the static
  shape_droplet_background drawable regardless of the shape_style
  setting. Now routed through IconStyleHelper.pillBackground like the
  other status-driven icons, keeping its semantic error colors.

- The tutorial/starter header icons (AdbPairingTutorialActivity,
  ShellTutorialActivity, StarterActivity) never applied icon
  style/color settings, so a shared-element transition from a styled
  Home card would visibly snap the icon's shape/color back to the
  static default mid-animation. Now styled with the same seedKey as
  their originating Home card so the transition lands on a consistent
  look.

- apps_activity.xml (both the manager and core/ui module copies, used
  by ApplicationManagementActivity and ActivityLogActivity) included a
  header_card that neither activity ever populated - rendering an
  empty, unlabeled colored blob at the top of both screens. Removed
  the dead include.

Fix cards blending into the background on Home and Settings

Both home_item_container.xml and M3ECardItemDecoration used a flat,
zero-elevation/zero-stroke card (Material 3's "Filled Card" look) but
filled it with colorSurfaceContainerLow - the tone meant for shadow-
backed "Elevated Card"s, only one subtle tonal step above the page
background. Switched both to colorSurfaceContainerHigh, matching the
same flat-card-that-pops pattern already used in swipe_hint_overlay.xml
and layout_settings_search_header.xml. Updated ThemeOverlay.Black to
keep AMOLED cards dialed down a step, same as it already did for the
old token.

Also fixed the top-level Settings screen (Capabilities/Personalization/

fix: stop AICore+ accessibility service from being disabled by OEM power managers (#320)

Two root causes behind "AICore+ enabled but accessibility always disabled after a short while"
on Samsung/OneUI:

1. The service subscribed to typeWindowContentChanged - the highest-frequency accessibility
   event, fired device-wide on every UI change - but its onAccessibilityEvent is empty and
   nothing (manager or server) ever consumes events; it only reads rootInActiveWindow on demand
   via the binder bridge. That constant cross-app wakeup is exactly the background-activity
   signal Samsung's watchdog uses to put the app to sleep and disable its accessibility service.
   Dropped the subscription to typeWindowStateChanged only (kept for OEM compatibility; still
   never consumed) and raised notificationTimeout. rootInActiveWindow / dispatchGesture don't
   depend on event subscription, so automation is unaffected.

2. Added AICoreAccessibilityHealer: on app foreground (MainActivity.onStart), if AICore+ is
   toggled on in-app and the manager holds WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS (post-Shizuku-start) but the
   service isn't in ENABLED_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICES, re-enable it via Settings.Secure - the same
   mechanism the ADB-pairing service already uses. Opportunistic only (no background watchdog),
   so it never fights a user who deliberately turned it off and adds zero wakeups.

Needs on-device confirmation on a Samsung device that the re-enable write isn't blocked by an
OEM restriction; safe if it is (self-heal is wrapped, worst case the user re-enables manually).

fix: retry binder delivery to clients whose provider wasn't ready on first push (#319)

BinderSender's process/uid observers added a pid/uid to their processed-set BEFORE calling
sendBinder() and ignored its result. sendBinderToUserApp() returns false when the target app's
ShizukuProvider isn't reachable yet - which routinely happens on the very first foreground event
of an app launch, before its ContentProvider is published (a startup race). Because the pid was
already recorded as handled and never removed, that single failed push was cached for the whole
process lifetime, leaving the app permanently "not registered" / "Shizuku not detected" until it
was force-killed and relaunched - a plausible contributor to the recurring reports on #319.

sendBinder() now returns whether the pid/uid can be remembered (not a Shizuku client, or binder
delivered); on a failed delivery to an actual client the observer drops it from the processed-set
so a later foreground/state-change event retries. Retries are event-driven and bounded (no loop
or timer), and duplicate delivery is harmless (idempotent). Manager delivery is unchanged - it
keeps its own kill-and-retry path and is always treated as handled.

Unverified on-device (no ADB device / SDK in this environment); watch the Build App CI run.

fix: backup key must accept device credential, not just biometric (#332/#315)

Follow-up to de56f144, which only changed the first symptom. A reporter on the new build got
IllegalBlockSizeException instead of "Key permanently invalidated". Root cause: BiometricLock
allows BIOMETRIC_STRONG | DEVICE_CREDENTIAL, but CryptoUtils created the auth-required key with a
bare setUserAuthenticationRequired(true), which on API 30+ defaults to biometric-only. So a
password/PIN-locked device with no biometric enrolled passes canAuthenticate, authenticates with
its credential, but that credential can't unlock the biometric-only key - and the AndroidKeyStore
surfaces that as IllegalBlockSizeException("Key user not authenticated") at doFinal.

Fix: on API 30+, create the key with setUserAuthenticationParameters(0, AUTH_BIOMETRIC_STRONG |
AUTH_DEVICE_CREDENTIAL) so it accepts whatever authenticator the device actually has, matching
BiometricLock. Timeout 0 keeps the per-use CryptoObject flow intact. Bumped the auth-key alias to
_v2 so the corrected key replaces the old biometric-only one for existing users (old keys can't be
re-parameterized in place). The _no_auth key (devices without a secure lock) is untouched.

Cost: auth-protected backups created before this fix can't be restored - but that path was already
broken on non-biometric devices, so real loss is minimal. de56f144's regenerate-on-invalidation
stays as the fallback for later screen-lock removal. Pre-API-30 keeps the legacy biometric-only
binding (BiometricLock already forces BIOMETRIC_STRONG there).

fix: Android 17 support - local-network perms, hidden-API compat shims, mDNS-resolved pairing host

Batched fixes so third-party apps and ADB pairing work on Android 17 (SDK 37),
verified against thedjchi's field-tested A17 fork:

1. Local Network Protection (#317): Android 16+ gates mDNS discovery of the
   wireless-debugging service and the loopback socket behind ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK
   (A17) / NEARBY_WIFI_DEVICES (A16). Added the manifest permissions and a tiered
   LocalNetworkPermission helper; AdbPairingTutorialActivity now requests it before
   starting the pairing service, StarterActivity before an ADB connect.

2. Hidden-API deviceId break: Android 17 inserted a deviceId param into
   IPackageManager/IPermissionManager (getPackageInfo/getApplicationInfo/
   checkPermission/grant/revoke) and changed getInstalledPackages' return type, so
   rikka's PackageManagerApis/PermissionManagerApis throw NoSuchMethodError -> no
   authorized apps show and permission grants fail. Added Android17Compat +
   InstalledPackagesCompat shims in :common (visible to server, server-shared and
   manager) that call the rikka wrapper first and fall back to raw reflection with
   deviceId=0; rerouted every affected server + manager call site.

3. mDNS-resolved pairing host: AdbMdns now surfaces the resolved host (normalized so
   loopback stays 127.0.0.1 - byte-identical to before; only a non-loopback local
   interface, as can happen under LNP, is used) so pairing connects to the real host
   instead of assuming loopback.

fix: self-heal manager uid so the manager isn't rejected as 'not manager' (SHIZUKUPLUS-6A)

managerAppId was resolved once at server startup and cached in a final field.
If that resolve was stale or failed - the manager app was reinstalled and got
a new uid, or the initial lookup raced the package manager / hit an Android-17
hidden-API miss on pre-r2129 builds - the server rejected its own manager with

manager-only call) failed indefinitely.

fix: home 'authorized apps' count no longer clobbered to 0 by a stale concurrent load (#317)

AppsViewModel.load() launches a fresh Dispatchers.IO coroutine every call, and
it's invoked from several places at once (the RUNNING state listener and
onResume() both call it). Overlapping passes each compute the granted count and
postValue in nondeterministic order, so an earlier pass that computed 0 (server
not ready yet, or a just-applied grant not yet propagated) could land AFTER the
correct count and leave the home card showing '0 authorized apps' until the list
was reopened — exactly what @Scoop2389 reported on #317 (0 after reboot / after
toggle-all, correct only on the next open).

Guard each pass with a monotonic generation token: a pass posts its result only
if no newer load() has started since it began, so the freshest count always wins.

Third-party stock Shizuku-API clients (App-Ops managers, Obtainium, etc.)

grant silently failed because no installed package DEFINED the name — the

- Compat Hub (moe.shizuku.privileged.api) now defines it dangerous, mirroring
  stock; safe because it shares stock's package name (mutually exclusive).
- Flavor-scope the manager: dropin (moe.shizuku.privileged.api) defines it
  natively — it IS the stock replacement and cannot host the Compat Hub —
  while shizukuplus (af.shizuku.plus.api) still removes it and delegates to
  the Compat Hub, preserving #316 coexistence with stock Shizuku.

  authority (detection is pingBinder() + package-name presence), so it was
  inert dead code.

pre-fix grant is not retried automatically), and the Plus flavor requires the

Detect server version skew and prompt to restart after an app update

When Shizuku+ updates, the privileged server keeps running the OLD code until
it's manually restarted (it's a separate long-lived process). If the binder wire
protocol differs between versions, third-party app connections can silently break
until the service is restarted — the residual cause behind "app X stopped working
after I updated" reports.

Detect it app-side, no protocol/server change:
- Record the app's versionCode whenever a server start is initiated. Every start
  path (AdbStarter, ShizukuReceiverStarter, tile, StarterActivity) funnels through
  ShizukuStateMachine STARTING, so recording on that transition captures all of
  them centrally.
- ShizukuStateMachine.isServerVersionSkewed() = running && startedBuild in
  1 until VERSION_CODE (false when unknown or current — no false positives).
- HomeActivity shows an indefinite snackbar (once per instance) when skewed, with
  a Restart action that stops the stale server; the home UI then offers the normal
  Start flow, launching a fresh server on the current build.

Fix SU Bridge for third-party apps: authenticate as the caller, not Shizuku+

The exported su/rish/plus wrappers hardcoded RISH_APPLICATION_ID=af.shizuku.plus.api.
But rish/app_process runs in the CALLING app's UID, and the Shizuku+ server's
attachApplication() throws SecurityException unless RISH_APPLICATION_ID belongs to
that calling UID (server/.../ShizukuService.java:339). So the bridge could only ever
work for Shizuku+ itself — every third-party app (Swift Backup, etc.) was rejected
with "Request package af.shizuku.plus.api does not belong to uid <app>". This is why
the Root Compatibility / SU Bridge never worked with real apps.

Fix: derive RISH_APPLICATION_ID from the calling app by walking up the process tree
to the first ancestor whose name looks like a package id, only when it isn't already
set. Applied in rish (the shared loader, so su inherits it) and the plus helper;
removed the hardcoded value from su.

Note: still requires the calling app to be authorized in Shizuku+, and the su path to
be invoked from an exec-permitted location (or via `sh <path>`); needs on-device
verification with Swift Backup.

Harden SU Bridge: deploy to /data/local/tmp + robust su arg parsing

Research (rikka rish docs + Android 14 behavior) confirmed the two remaining blockers
after the RISH_APPLICATION_ID fix are (1) shared storage is usually mounted noexec, so
apps can't exec the su path from the storage export, and (2) app_process rejects a
writable dex on Android 14+ and FAT/exFAT SD cards can't hold unix perms at all.

- RootCompatHelper.deployBridgeToTmp(): stream su/rish/plus (0755) + rish_shizuku.dex
  (0444) to /data/local/tmp over the privileged process's stdin (`cat > file`), which is
  exec-permitted and works in both root and ADB mode (no cross-UID file read). autoSetupAll
  now deploys there and configures apps to point at /data/local/tmp/su; the Root Compat
  screen deploys on open and prefers that path for copy/display, falling back to storage.
- su wrapper: parse arguments robustly — everything after -c is the command (not just the
  first token), and a leading user specifier (root/0/<name>) or unmappable flags
  (--mount-master, -s, -p, ...) are skipped. Handles more apps' su invocation styles.

Note: for apps that support Shizuku *directly* (e.g. Swift Backup), that native path is
preferred over the su bridge. Still needs on-device verification.

Gives users a concrete pass/fail before they wire up a target app, and reports
the REAL privilege ceiling instead of the spoofed one. Two probes:

  since that runs at the server's uid which owns no app package). If a ROM's
  SELinux blocks an untrusted app from exec'ing app_process / reading
  shell_data_file in /data/local/tmp, we report that honestly — it's real signal
  that exec-style callers won't work on that device, not a bridge bug.

fix(server): stop catastrophic-guard from blocking legit deletes under /data etc.

isCatastrophicCommand runs on every newProcess and used loose substring
matching: contains("rm -rf /data" | "rm -rf /storage" | "rm -rf /system").

(SecurityException) on very common app operations:

  rm -rf /storage/emulated/0/Android/data/<pkg>/files/tmp
  rm -rf /data/local/tmp/...        <- including the SU bridge's OWN cleanup

whose target is a partition ROOT as a complete path token — /data, /system,
/storage, /vendor, /sdcard, or /, optionally with a trailing "/*" glob —
requiring end-of-string or whitespace after it so /data/data/... and
/data_backup are NOT matched. Verified against a block/allow battery
(whole-partition wipes still blocked; subpath and targeted-file deletes,
e.g. debloating /system/app/Foo.apk, now allowed).

fix(server): don't treat su -mm/--mount-master as an argument-taking flag

In the SU Bridge su-arg parser, -mm/--mount-master were grouped with flags
that consume a following token (-s, -cn, -g, -u). But Magisk's mount-master
flag is standalone — it takes no argument. So `su -mm -c "cmd"` set
skipNext=true on -mm, which ate the -c; the actual command was then treated
as a positional user arg and dropped, leaving an empty interactive `sh`.
Result: any mount-master invocation (common via libsu) silently ran nothing.

Move -mm/--mount-master to the no-argument Magisk-mode branch so they're
skipped without consuming the next token.

fix(server): record package names on toggle-authorize, not just the dialog path (#337)

updateFlagsForUid() - the code path behind the normal app-list toggle switch,
used for the vast majority of authorizations - called
configManager.update(uid, null, mask, value), never recording which package(s)
the uid actually covers. Only dispatchPermissionConfirmationResult() (the
separate interactive permission-request dialog flow) populated real package
names.

That empty packages list was silently destructive in two places that both
treat "no recorded packages" as "matches nothing" instead of "nothing
recorded yet":

- getApplications()'s per-package membership filter excluded the package
  from the authorized-apps list entirely on the very next list refresh
  (Preference.contains() on an empty list is always false) - matching
  reports of an authorized app "disappearing" and the authorized count
  dropping, without the OS-level grant itself ever having failed.
- ShizukuConfigManager's startup reconciliation treated the empty list as
  proof the uid's packages changed and pruned the whole entry on every
  server restart - so on OEMs that kill/restart the Shizuku+ server more
  aggressively, this would recur indefinitely, surviving re-toggles (each
  re-toggle recreated the same unpopulated entry).

Fixes: pass the real package list through to configManager.update() from
updateFlagsForUid(); treat an empty entry.packages as "unrestricted, never
recorded" rather than "restricted to nothing" in both the membership filter
and the reconciliation pass, and backfill it from the live package list
in-place so existing broken entries self-heal on the next server restart
without requiring every affected user to manually re-toggle.

fix(backup): explain un-decryptable restores instead of minting a doomed key (#370)

Restoring a settings backup after uninstall/reinstall (or after clearing app
data) failed opaquely. getCipherForDecryption called getOrCreateSecretKey,
which — when the AndroidKeyStore alias was gone — silently minted a BRAND-NEW
key. doFinal() then blew up with a bare AEADBadTagException and left a useless
orphan key in the keystore. The user just saw "Restore failed: AEADBadTag..."
with no idea why.

The root cause is by design: the backup key is a non-exportable, hardware-backed
keystore key that Android destroys on uninstall / data-clear, so a backup can
only ever be restored by the installation that created it.

- CryptoUtils.getCipherForDecryption now checks for the key up front and throws
  a clear BackupKeyUnavailableException instead of creating a doomed key.
- backupErrorMessage() maps both BackupKeyUnavailableException and
  AEADBadTagException to plain-language explanations (backup is per-install;
  can't be restored after reinstall / on another device / if tampered with).

Does NOT make backups portable across installs — that needs password-derived
encryption (a separate, testable change). This stops the confusing failure and
the orphan-key side effect.

fix(su-bridge): resolve two-segment packages (com.termux) in rish/plus (#368,#372)

The process-tree walk that discovers the calling app's package (to set
RISH_APPLICATION_ID) matched on the glob `*.*.*`, which requires THREE
dot-separated segments. Common packages have only two — most importantly
`com.termux` — so the walk never resolved them: RISH_APPLICATION_ID stayed
unset, app_process attached with no package id, and the Shizuku+ server
rejected the attach. That surfaced as rish "silently timing out" in Termux
(#368) and Termux never appearing as a client (#372/#374).

Fix the match in both rish and plus:
  - skip any candidate containing a slash first (`*/*`) — those are paths or
    binaries like /data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin/bash, never a package;
  - then match one-or-more dots (`*.*`), so two-segment ids like com.termux
    resolve while the walk still climbs past intermediate shells/binaries.

Verified with `sh -n` and a case-match harness: com.termux and com.whatsapp
now resolve, the Termux bash path and /system/bin/sh are skipped, and
multi-segment ids (org.swiftapps.swiftbackup) still match as before.

Note: users who manually copied an older rish into their terminal must re-copy
it (or re-run the in-app deploy) to pick up the fix.

fix(privileged): use StringBuffer in the shared capture helper to avoid a data race

ShizukuProcessUtils.runPrivilegedCapture drains stdout/stderr on background
threads into StringBuilders, but reads them via toString() on the caller thread

Fix Drop-In UserService start: hardcoded manager package broke every start (#371)

ServiceStarter.sendBinder() hardcoded "af.shizuku.plus.api" as the
manager's ContentProvider authority when handing a freshly-spawned
UserService's binder back to the manager. ServiceStarter runs in its own
app_process, spawned fresh per UserService, so it has no visibility into
ShizukuService's runtime-resolved ServerConstants.MANAGER_APPLICATION_ID
(which correctly flips to moe.shizuku.privileged.api on a Drop-In-only
install - see ShizukuService.getManagerApplicationInfo()).

The manager's dropin flavor manifest declares its provider authority as
${applicationId}.shizuku, i.e. moe.shizuku.privileged.api.shizuku - which
never matched the hardcoded af.shizuku.plus.api.shizuku ServiceStarter
was looking for. Every UserService start (which is most of what
third-party apps actually do through Shizuku - see rikka.appops, Hail,
Tasker, MiXplorer, LinkSheet in #371) failed unconditionally on Drop-In
with "provider is null af.shizuku.plus.api.shizuku 0", exactly matching
the logcat gmm96 and Paul-max-000 posted on #371.

Fix: thread the server's already-resolved MANAGER_APPLICATION_ID through
to ServiceStarter as a --manager= CLI arg, same way --package/--token/
--class are already passed across the process boundary.

Confirmed this isn't an upstream-vs-fork regression: upstream Shizuku's
ServiceStarter also hardcodes its provider package name, but upstream
only ever ships one application id, so it never needed to vary. The
dual-flavor (Plus + Drop-In sharing one server binary) architecture is
ShizukuPlus-specific, and this is the one place that dynamic resolution
wasn't threaded through when Drop-In was added.

Fix rish on Drop-In + extend freezer guard to reentrant callback (#371)

Two more fixes from a deeper investigation into #371:

1. rish/plus shell entry point (ShizukuShellLoader.requestForBinder) hardcoded
   "af.shizuku.plus.api" as the REQUEST_BINDER broadcast target - same bug class
   as the ServiceStarter.kt fix in bbcf4fd1. This process is spawned fresh via
   app_process by the rish/plus scripts, in the calling app's own UID, so it can't
   see the server's runtime-resolved manager package id. Intent.setPackage()
   silently drops the broadcast when the named package isn't installed, so on a
   Drop-In-only install rish always timed out after 15s with a misleading
   "connection may be blocked by your system" message. Now resolves the installed
   flavor dynamically (Plus first, then Drop-In), mirroring
   ShizukuService.getManagerApplicationInfo()'s own fallback logic. Likely the
   root cause of #377.

2. Extends the Cached-Apps-Freezer guard (api submodule commit de71666) to
   ShizukuService.attachApplication()'s own reentrant application.bindApplication()
   callback - the best match for #371's exact logcat signature ("sent binder code
   1 ... to frozen apps and got error -74": code=1 + oneway is
   IShizukuApplication.bindApplication precisely).

Bumps the api submodule pointer to de71666, which also carries the equivalent
guard for ClientRecord.dispatchRequestPermissionResult and
UserServiceManager.addUserService's broadcastBinderReceived call sites.

OEM builds (e.g. Samsung One UI on the S25) the startActivity call is
silently dropped, so the consent dialog never appears and
ShizukuShellLoader's 15s timeout fires with a misleading "may be blocked by
your system / disable battery optimization" message. Post a high-priority
notification instead and open ShellConsentActivity from its content
PendingIntent - tapping a notification is a user-initiated foreground
action and is exempt from BAL, so the dialog now reliably shows up.

POST_NOTIFICATIONS granted - and that permission was previously only ever
requested from the ADB pairing tutorial flow, so anyone who set up the
service via root/PC mode, or who paired ADB before ever opening that
screen, never got asked. The result reproduces the exact original symptom
(rish silently times out) with no visible cause, which is what the
original #377 reporter hit again after updating.

fix: don't let rish's client timeout race a successful consent grant (#377)

ShizukuShellLoader's abort timer was a fixed, uncancelled 15s
postDelayed - sized (per the commit that introduced it) for the
consent dialog launching directly. Since then, the dialog is routed
through a notification the user has to notice, open, and tap first to
dodge Android's background-activity-launch restrictions, and that
extra human step was never budgeted for. brandonmathewp's #377 retest
shows the full flow succeeding (notification fires, tap works, consent
granted) and rish *still* times out - the grant simply arrives after
the client has already self-terminated on a clock nothing resets.

Cancel the callback the moment onBinderReceived() actually fires, and
bump the fallback timeout to 90s so a slow-but-successful interaction
has real margin instead of racing a budget calibrated for the old flow.

fix: catch up already-running clients at server start (#371)

BinderSender's ProcessObserver/UidObserver only fire on a *transition*
(foreground, uid active/idle/cached, process died/started). A client
that's already running - and possibly already frozen - at the exact
moment the server (re)starts never produces one of those transitions
on its own, so it would sit waiting indefinitely for some unrelated
later state change instead of getting the binder it's owed right away.

This mirrors what Stellar does for the same problem, but takes a
different path to it: Stellar walks raw running processes via
reflection on a hidden IActivityManager method that isn't exposed by
dev.rikka.hidden:compat (the vetted hidden-API library this project
already depends on everywhere else). Instead of introducing new
unvetted reflection, this inverts the enumeration - walk installed
packages that declare the Shizuku permission (an API this codebase
already uses in ShizukuConfigManager/getApplications), and check each
one's live process state via ActivityManagerApis.getPackageProcessState
(already exposed by the same compat library) before delivering.

The process-state check matters: without it, this would resolve a
ContentProvider for every authorized package regardless of whether
it's actually running, which can force-start it - turning "catch up
already-running clients" into "launch every authorized app on every
server boot." Skipping on any unexpected/unreadable state fails closed
rather than risking that.

client except the manager in 827e1d27 ("improve startup speed") -
upstream RikkaApps/Shizuku still has this for all clients. Ordinary
clients (Hail, App Ops, WifiList, Tasker, ...) are delivered through
this exact synchronous ContentProvider call via BinderSender and
ShizukuService.sendBinderToClient's startup catch-up, with no
recovery when the target's provider looks dead - which is what a
frozen target's binder does from the caller's side. Added
sendBinderToUserAppWithRetry (force-stop + one delayed retry,
mirroring sendBinderToManager's existing pattern) and wired both
call sites to use it.

callback, which had the identical freezer race acknowledged in its

sendBinderToUserAppWithRetry's force-stop-and-retry is only safe where
the target can't plausibly be mid-operation. BinderSender.sendBinder()
fires on every foreground/process-state/uid observer event during live
usage, not just at startup - a transient pingBinder() false-positive
there force-stops a live, possibly busy app. Reported after r2211:
Morphe got force-stopped mid-package-install ("Failed to install
update: ...IPackageInstaller.asBinder() on a null object reference"),
consistent with its process getting killed out from under an in-flight
PackageInstaller session.

where a client can't have an operation in flight since Shizuku wasn't
available moments earlier. The existing #319 un-cache-on-failure
handling remains the safety net for the live path.

fix: store shell consent binder in-memory, fix TOCTOU and stomp bugs (#387)

Android 15+ (API 35) does not reliably deliver IBinder objects embedded in
PendingIntent extras — the binder arrives null when ShellConsentActivity reads
it, so rish hangs indefinitely after the user taps Allow.

Fix by introducing PendingConsentStore: an in-memory singleton that holds the
callback binder keyed by UUID. BinderRequestReceiver stores the binder there
and passes only the key in the notification intent (no IBinder crosses the
PendingIntent boundary at all). ShellConsentActivity takes the binder eagerly
in onCreate via PendingConsentStore.take(), which also:

- Eliminates the TOCTOU between a peek() existence-check and a later take() in
  handleRequest (binder death between those two calls silently discarded grants)
- Removes the 'take-before-transact loses the binder on exception' hazard by
  giving ShellConsentActivity ownership of the binder before the dialog opens
- Fixes concurrent-request key stomp: PendingIntent.getActivity() now uses
  consentKey.hashCode() as the requestCode instead of the hardcoded 0, so
  concurrent rish invocations each get their own PendingIntent slot
- put() now returns null when linkToDeath throws (binder already dead) so the
  notification is not posted for a request that can never be fulfilled

Also splits ShellBinderRequestHandler into handleRequest() (auth-token fast
path, reads binder from intent) and deliverBinder() (notification consent path,
takes a pre-resolved binder), so the consent flow no longer needs to call
through the handler's store-lookup logic at all.

fix(#391): rish shell always treated as unidentified — UID fallback chain

Root cause: the consent flow (notification label, grant persistence, fast-path
check) relied entirely on PackageManager.getApplicationInfo(callingPackage) to
resolve the caller's UID. When callingPackage is absent (classic rish_shizuku.dex
does not include it) or when PM lookup fails on certain devices, callingUid is
null throughout and AuthorizationManager.grant() is never called. Every new rish
invocation therefore falls through to the notification consent path and the
"Allow always" tap grants nothing, so the next run re-prompts.

Fix:
- ShizukuShellLoader always includes Os.getuid() as the "callingUid" extra in
  the REQUEST_BINDER broadcast. This process runs as the caller's UID, so the
  value is authoritative.
- BinderRequestReceiver, ShellConsentActionReceiver, and ShellConsentActivity
  now use a UID fallback chain: PM-derived UID (verifies package ownership) →
  intent callingUid → no grant. All grant and granted() calls use whichever
  UID is available.
- postConsentNotification threads callingUid through all PendingIntent extras
  (consentIntent, allowIntent) so the UID is available when the user taps.
- postConsentNotification falls back to the package name string as appLabel
  when getApplicationInfo fails, so the notification/dialog shows a useful
  identifier rather than the generic "cannot be identified" text.

the consent notification entirely.

Broadcast Intent extras carry no verified sender identity -
Binder.getCallingUid() is not meaningful in onReceive() for a plain
sendBroadcast(), and REQUEST_BINDER is the public, unauthenticated part
of Shizuku's client API that any installed app can send. Any app could:

  1. Send REQUEST_BINDER with callingPackage="<any already-authorized
     package>" and its own callbackBinder in the "data" extra.
  2. The receiver resolved that package's real (public) UID via
     PackageManager and passed AuthorizationManager.granted() using
     that package's genuine prior grant.
  3. ShellBinderRequestHandler.deliverBinder() transacted the live,
     full-privilege Shizuku service binder directly into the attacker's
     own callbackBinder.

Zero user interaction required, as long as any app on the device had
ever been authorized (a near-universal state once Shizuku+ is set up).

Fix: the fast path is removed. Every request without a valid
cryptographic auth token (which a shell/rish process can never produce
by design) now always goes through the existing consent-notification
flow, which requires an explicit user tap before any binder is
delivered - the only trust boundary this architecture can actually
enforce for an unauthenticated broadcast. This reverts the #398
convenience (silently skipping the prompt for already-approved
callers); restoring it safely needs a different mechanism that doesn't
trust spoofable Intent extras (e.g. verification inside a real AIDL
transaction on the server, where Binder.getCallingUid() is reliable).

shell) performed it. This preserves the documented root<->shell
interop (root always bypasses DAC; shell is covered via the group
bit) while closing access to any third-party UID.

fix(security): re-implement always-allow persistence for shell/rish clients safely (#420, #416)

BinderRequestReceiver's no-token (rish/shell) path used to gate binder
delivery on a per-request consent notification, since a prior "skip if
already authorized" fast path (added for #398) was removed after it was
found to trust spoofable broadcast Intent extras (callingPackage/callingUid)
- any installed app could claim to be an already-authorized package and
silently receive the live Shizuku binder. That fix was correct but left
nothing to replace the skip logic, so every rish invocation re-prompted
forever regardless of a prior "Allow always" grant (#420, #416).

Fix: BinderRequestReceiver now delivers the binder unconditionally, making
no authorization decision at all. Receiving a bare binder reference isn't
the actual privilege boundary - every privileged AIDL method is separately
gated by enforceCallingPermission(), keyed off Binder.getCallingUid() from
the real transaction the caller makes once attached, not spoofable broadcast
extras. The one-time consent prompt (and persisted "allow always" grant) now
happens entirely through the existing, already uid-verified path:
attachApplication() -> checkSelfPermission() -> requestPermission() ->
showPermissionConfirmation() -> RequestPermissionActivity - which already
correctly skips prompting once a uid is granted.

That activity previously bailed silently when PackageManager couldn't
resolve the caller's ApplicationInfo (the same PM-lookup gap #391's fix
addressed elsewhere), leaving the caller's requestPermission() call hanging
forever with no dispatch. Fixed alongside this change (showPermissionConfirmation
+ RequestPermissionActivity) to fall back to a package-name/uid label
instead of dropping the request.

Removes the now-fully-dead notification-based consent machinery this
replaces: ShellConsentActivity, ShellConsentActionReceiver,
PendingConsentStore, and their manifest entries and strings.

fix: Watchdog can now recover from a full process freeze, not just a service crash (#415, #417)

Samsung One UI's "Sleeping apps" freezer (and similar OEM battery
managers) can kill the ENTIRE manager process on screen lock, not
just WatchdogService - and a dead/frozen process can't detect its
own death, so nothing running inside it (WatchdogService's state-flow
listener, WatchdogWorker's WorkManager backstop) can ever notice or
recover. The only prior "fix" for this (a519414c) was a diagnostic
honesty fix in Service Doctor, not an actual recovery mechanism -
confirmed via review before touching this.

Added WatchdogAlarmReceiver: an AlarmManager.setExactAndAllowWhileIdle
re-arm, self-rescheduling every 15 minutes, that survives a full
process kill because it's dispatched by system_server rather than
anything inside the app's own process - the same trick other apps use
to survive OEM freezers. Falls back to an inexact wake if the
SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM permission is declined or restricted.

Wired into setWatchdog() (enable/disable - see prior commit),
BootCompleteReceiver (exact alarms don't survive reboot), and
ShizukuApplication.onCreate() (covers any other process-start path).

This is a mitigation bounded by the 15-minute interval, not a
complete fix for aggressive OEM freezers - documented as such in the
wiki (Service-Connection#watchdog) and Permissions page.

fix: release tag push rejected by GitHub since the default token can't touch workflow-modifying history

Every CI run since this session's own .github/workflows/app.yml edits
landed has failed at the "Create Release Tag" step:

  ! [remote rejected] vX.Y.Z -> vX.Y.Z (refusing to allow a GitHub App
  to create or update workflow `.github/workflows/app.yml` without
  `workflows` permission)

The default GITHUB_TOKEN can't push any ref - including a plain
release tag - once the commit history it's reachable from touches
.github/workflows/. There's no "workflows" permission key that can be
granted to it via the workflow's own `permissions:` block; only a PAT
with the `workflow` scope can push past this. Since that
workflow-editing commit is now permanent history, this broke every
future release, not just the one that introduced it.

Fixed by pushing the release tag via an explicit authenticated URL
using a new `RELEASE_PAT` repo secret (repo + workflow scope),
provided by the maintainer, instead of relying on the checkout's
default-token-authenticated `origin` remote. Scoped to just this one
push - nothing else in the workflow uses it.

fix: SecurityException crash from haptic feedback on HyperOS/MIUI (SHIZUKUPLUS-8E)

View.performHapticFeedback() doesn't need VIBRATE on stock AOSP, but HyperOS/
MIUI's haptics stack (miui.util.HapticFeedbackUtil -> VibrateUtils.vibrate)
routes through the real vibrator service and enforces the permission, so
every haptic call in HapticUtils was crashing with a SecurityException on
those OEMs whenever the user touched a haptic-triggering control. Declared
VIBRATE (normal-protection, auto-granted, no runtime prompt) so it actually
works, and wrapped every call in a SecurityException guard as a backstop -
haptics are decorative and should never be able to crash the app regardless
of what a given OEM's implementation does underneath.

feat: adopt AppCompatDelegate.setApplicationLocales() as locale source of truth (#429)

Fixes the disagreement between this app's in-app language picker and
Android 13+'s system "App language" settings screen: the app declared
android:localeConfig (making that system screen appear) but never told
AppCompatDelegate about locale changes, and vice versa - picking a
language in-app didn't update the system screen, and picking one via the
system screen wouldn't have been honored by the app at all.

- AndroidManifest.xml: added AppLocalesMetadataHolderService with
  autoStoreLocales=true, the standard AppCompat mechanism for per-app
  language persistence pre-API 33.
- ShizukuSettings: one-time migration flag + a raw (non-collapsed)
  language-tag accessor, so the existing legacy locale preference can be
  handed off to AppCompatDelegate exactly once.
- ShizukuApplication.onCreate(): performs that one-time handoff.
- PersonalizationSettingsFragment: the language picker now calls
  AppCompatDelegate.setApplicationLocales() instead of only
  LocaleDelegate.defaultLocale + an app-driven recreateWithoutTransition()
  - avoids double-recreating the activity, since setApplicationLocales()
  triggers its own recreate.
- AppActivity.attachBaseContext() (core/ui, our own base class every
  Activity extends): the actual fix that makes AppCompatDelegate genuinely
  authoritative. MaterialActivity (rikka's base class AppActivity
  extends) forces the activity's locale to LocaleDelegate.defaultLocale
  on every single attachBaseContext call - without re-syncing that value
  from AppCompatDelegate first, a system-Settings-initiated locale change
  would get silently reverted on the very next screen. This was caught by
  an adversarial review pass before it shipped; the first implementation
  attempt only wrote to AppCompatDelegate without ever reading from it,
  so MaterialActivity's read would have kept winning.

Also fixed a pre-existing, unrelated bug discovered while implementing
the above: AppActivity's edge-to-edge/Blur UI preference reads used
getSharedPreferences("${packageName}_preferences", ...) - the plain
default-storage file - but ShizukuSettings actually stores these in a
device-protected-storage file named "settings"
(createDeviceProtectedStorageContext()). The two files never contained
the same data, so those reads always silently fell back to their default
values: edge-to-edge could never actually be turned off, and Blur UI
could never actually be turned on. Fixed both reads to use the correct
storage context/filename (verified against ShizukuSettings.getPreferences()'s
actual implementation, not assumed).

Also includes Samsung DeX process-keepalive meta-data (developer.samsung.
com/samsung-dex/modify-optimizing.html) - unrelated to locale handling,
bundled here since both are AndroidManifest.xml <application> additions.

Tracked in #429.

feat: add "Cut (Angular)" shape style, a genuinely new silhouette not just a radius change

M3 Expressive's stated "Embrace Tension" principle mixes sharp/angular
forms with soft/rounded ones - the existing 4 shape styles (Zen/Modern/
Classic/Organic) all use the ROUNDED corner family at different radii,
so they're variations on one silhouette. This adds a 5th style using the
CUT corner family (stable ShapeAppearance API, not experimental) for
cards/containers, plus a matching octagon icon-background pill
(GradientDrawable has no native cut-corner support, so this is a small

Researched Google's actual M3 Expressive shape library (MaterialShapes -
cookie/sunny/clover/pill polygon morphing, androidx.compose.material3)
as the more ambitious version of this ask: it's Compose-only (Canvas/
RoundedPolygon, no ShapeAppearanceModel/MaterialCardView equivalent) and

adopting it doesn't fit this mostly-XML-View app without either a much

fix: ShizukuStateMachine.update() misreported crashes as intentional stops, silently defeating the #417 watchdog re-arm

Root cause: update()'s fallback when Shizuku.pingBinder() finds the binder
dead only preserved STARTING/STOPPING/CRASHED from the current state - a
prior RUNNING state fell through to `else -> STOPPED`. WatchdogService's
flow collector only restarts the server on a CRASHED transition, so any
unexpected death update() detected (rather than the in-process
addBinderDeadListener) was silently reclassified as an intentional stop
and never triggered a restart.

This made WatchdogAlarmReceiver's external, process-independent re-arm
(landed in c6a76f3f for #415/#417) inert for its primary purpose: a
cold-started process after an OEM freezer kill has no in-memory record of
the prior RUNNING state either (defaults to STOPPED), so even the "was it
running" check itself was blind across a process restart.

Fix: persist the last settled state (RUNNING/STOPPED/CRASHED) via
ShizukuSettings whenever transition() commits one, seed the in-memory
state from that persisted value instead of a hardcoded STOPPED default,
and add the missing `currentState == RUNNING -> CRASHED` branch in
update(). Deliberate stops still settle to STOPPED via the existing
STOPPING path and persist correctly, so this doesn't cause the watchdog
to "restart" something the user turned off.

Found via live on-device verification: confirmed shizuku_plus_server
died and silently stayed dead (app showed "Shizuku is not running")
despite the server process itself getting cold-restarted, matching
reports across #371/#424/#389 of Shizuku+ going silent after backgrounding
with no user-visible recovery.

fix: force-stop an already-connected app when its authorization is granted, so it picks up the new grant

Root cause: updateFlagsForUid() (the Application Management screen's
authorize toggle) updated the server-side ClientRecord.allowed flag and
the OS-level runtime permission, but never told an already-connected
client anything changed. Shizuku.checkSelfPermission()'s cached
permissionGranted field is only ever populated from attachApplication()'s
reply, and there's no protocol-level way to push a correction to a live
client afterward: dispatchRequestPermissionResult needs a caller-chosen
requestCode tied to an active requestPermission() call we were never
given, and re-sending the same server binder is a client-side no-op
(onBinderReceived() short-circuits on `binder == newBinder`).

So an app that connected once before being authorized (common on devices
that auto-launch apps early, e.g. on boot) stayed stuck showing "not
granted" indefinitely after being granted from Shizuku+'s own UI, until
manually force-stopped and relaunched.

Fix: on grant, force-stop the package if it was previously denied - the
same mechanism the revoke branch immediately below already relies on as
the only reliable way to make a live client observe a permission change.
Guarded on `!record.allowed` so an already-granted, already-working app
isn't disrupted by a redundant re-toggle.

Found via direct comparison of two screenshots from #371 (LSPatch shown
authorized in Shizuku+'s own Application Management screen while LSPatch
itself reported "Shizuku is running but I don't have access" - working
correctly on an older build, broken on the current one). Not yet
confirmed against the reporter's device.

Same conflict class as b392c8f3, found by auditing every place that
mutates ClientRecord.allowed for the same pattern: a live client-state

own connection time until manually killed and relaunched.

actually changes, matching the mechanism the revoke path in
updateFlagsForUid() already established as the only reliable way to make
a live client observe a permission change it wasn't itself waiting on.

fix: settings put optimization no longer short-circuits native execution (#452)

The 'Plus Optimization' for `settings put` intercepted ALL settings put
commands, wrote via ContentProvider fast-path, then returned true without
ever running the real shell command. On Samsung Android 16 (and other OEMs
that tighten secure-settings access), callCompat() can complete silently
while the system rejects the actual write — causing apps like Essential by
sameerasw to get a success exit code but see no effect when toggling
settings like "Hide all system icons".

Changed from an early return to a best-effort pre-write: the ContentProvider
call still executes for performance, but the code falls through to
super.newProcessInternal(cmd) which runs the authoritative native shell
command regardless of whether the fast path succeeded.

fix: persist adb_tcp_port to Settings.Global for rootless boot reconnect (#454)

After a successful tcpip:PORT handshake, write adb_tcp_port to
Settings.Global so adbd binds it on the next boot without needing
Wireless Debugging or Wi-Fi — the same mechanism other Shizuku forks
use. WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS is already held by the ADB shell that
granted Shizuku in the first place, so no root is required.

AdbStartWorker gains a fast-path that fires before mDNS: if TCP mode
is on and WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS is available, write adb_tcp_port, wait
600ms for adbd, then probe the port. If it responds, skip mDNS entirely
and connect directly, avoiding the 15s discovery timeout on reboot.

fix: skip UID→package check when PackageManager returns empty list (#444)

On Samsung OneUI 8 and other OEMs with aggressive process caching, PM can
return an empty package list for a UID during the brief post-reboot window
before the package scan completes. Throwing a SecurityException in that
case prevents attachApplication from adding a ClientRecord, so subsequent
newProcess() calls have no record and fail the permission check with a
null-message SecurityException — surfaces as "execViaShizuku failed: null"
in client apps (SamFonts, aShell You).

Skip the UID→package verification only when PM returns empty (transient
failure). The binder was already granted by BinderSender which only sends
to authorized UIDs; clientRecord.allowed remains the authoritative security
gate once attached.

fix: pipe compat.apk via stdin to avoid Android 11+ scoped storage block (#446)

On Android 11+, /sdcard/Android/data/<pkg>/ is blocked from shell UID
2000 (scoped storage), so the previous cp-then-pm-install approach
silently failed with "Permission denied" on Pixel 5, Pixel 6, Samsung
A40, and other Android 11+ devices. The generic error toast was shown
because the cp failure output didn't contain "INSTALL_FAILED" or
"Failure" to trigger the detail branch.

Fix for Shizuku path: pipe APK bytes directly from assets to the shell
process's stdin. The shell script uses `cat > /data/local/tmp/compat.apk`
which writes to world-accessible storage without touching any app-private
path. cat exits on EOF (when we close outputStream), then && chains into
pm install. No concurrent stdin/stdout needed — pm install only starts
after cat finishes, so there's no deadlock risk.

Fix for root path: extract APK bytes to internal cacheDir, which root
can read. Clean up in a finally block.

fix: auto-update install and compat hub Shizuku v11+ provider proxy

UpdateManager.installApk had two bugs that prevented auto-install from ever
working:
1. Shizuku-only path was using Shell.cmd() (root) to run pm install, but
   shell UID 2000 can't read getExternalFilesDir on Android 11+ scoped
   storage. Fixed by reading APK bytes in the app process and streaming
   them to pm install via Shizuku.newProcess() stdin (same pattern as
   compat hub install in 954dbc27).
2. context.startActivity(installIntent) silently fails on Android 10+
   from a background coroutine — the OS blocks background activity starts
   but throws no exception, so installApk returned true and
   showInstallNotification was never called. Fixed by removing the
   startActivity path entirely; installApk now returns false on any
   non-silent result, letting onDownloadComplete show the notification.

Compat hub: add ShizukuProviderProxy ContentProvider at authority
moe.shizuku.privileged.api.shizuku. Shizuku API v11+ apps call
ContentResolver.call() on this exact authority to retrieve the Shizuku
binder. Without this provider the compat hub only served legacy
broadcast-path (REQUEST_BINDER) clients; all modern v11+ apps (App Ops
managers, Obtainium, etc.) silently failed to connect. The proxy
forwards call() to af.shizuku.plus.api.shizuku where
ShizukuManagerProvider handles it.

fix: compat hub install fallback when Shizuku.newProcess() returns null

On Samsung One UI 8 / Android 16 and some Redmagic devices, Android's
SELinux policy blocks Shizuku's process-spawning API (newProcess()),
causing the compat hub install button to show the generic "Ensure
Shizuku+ is active" error even when the server is running fine.

Changed the Shizuku install path to distinguish between:
- newProcess() returning null (device restriction) → system installer
- newProcess() succeeding but pm install failing → existing error cases

When newProcess() returns null, the APK bytes (already in memory from
assets) are written to cacheDir and shared via FileProvider, then the
system installer activity is launched. The user sees a toast explaining
the device restriction and needs to tap through one system install
dialog. Previously this path showed a misleading "Ensure Shizuku+ is
active" error with no fallback.
