fix: prevent null IRemoteProcess crash in clients on Samsung OneUI 8 (#466)

Two changes in ShizukuService.newProcess():

1. Wrap the final super.newProcessInternal() fallback in try-catch — when
   SELinux blocks exec on Samsung OneUI 8, the base-class method throws
   instead of returning null. Without this catch, the exception propagates
   over Binder and the client (e.g. aShellYou) receives a null IRemoteProcess,
   crashing with NullPointerException on first use.

   in the same pattern — that early-return path was unreachable by the bottom-
   level guard, so it was the specific code path that triggered #466.

Both fall back to syntheticProcess(1, null) so callers see exit code 1 with
empty stdout rather than a null binder crash.

fix(automation): stabilize auth token verification (#467)

The extrasLayout in home_automation_bottom_sheet.xml already has
app:prefixText="auth: " as a visual label. AutomationViewHolder was
also prepending "auth:" to the EditText value, producing a double-
prefix in the displayed text ("auth:  auth:<base64>") and — critically
— copying "auth:<base64>" to the clipboard.

AuthenticatedReceiver strips the "auth:" prefix and passes the
remainder to IntentCrypto.decrypt(). When the remainder was
"auth:<base64>", Base64.decode() threw on the ':' character, decrypt()
returned null, and the fallback plaintext compare against the raw token
always failed — resulting in "Invalid auth token" for every user using
an encrypted token (the normal path on devices with AndroidKeyStore).

Fix: write only the bare base64 blob (or raw plaintext on OEMs where
AndroidKeyStore is unavailable) into extrasEditText. The visual "auth: "
label is already supplied by the layout prefix. Receivers already accept
bare base64 (no "auth:" prefix required) and continue to accept the old
"auth:<base64>" format for tokens copied before this fix.

Android 15+ (API 35, targetSdk 35) enforces edge-to-edge for all apps and

fix(security): clear Play Integrity verdict cache on wallet fix, not just force-stop

The previous refreshGoogleWalletAttestation only force-stopped Wallet, leaving
GMS's cached "compromised" verdict intact. Wallet would re-read that verdict on
the next launch and stay blocked, requiring a nuclear pm clear com.google.android.gms
(which wipes account state) to recover.

Root cause: Play Integrity verdicts are cached in GMS's DATA directory, not its
cache dir, so pm clear-cache and force-stop have no effect on them.

fix(security): correct Play Integrity cache refresh — ADB shell can't touch GMS data dir

Investigations via live ADB revealed three bugs in the previous commit:

1. `pm clear-cache` was removed in Android 10+ — returns "Unknown command" with exit 0,
   so the method silently no-oped while reporting success.
2. Shell (uid 2000) cannot read or write /data/data/com.google.android.gms/ — all rm
   commands failed with EACCES (redirected to /dev/null), yet we echoed OK and returned
   CACHE_CLEARED, which was a false positive shown to the user.
3. `com.google.android.gms.INITIALIZE` broadcast has no registered receivers — result=0,
   complete no-op; removed.

Fix:
- Split clearPlayIntegrityCache into clearPlayIntegrityCacheAsRoot (uid 0 only) which
  probes readability first and counts deleted files before claiming success, and a no-op
  path for ADB shell mode.
- Add explicit Shizuku UID check: root mode does targeted file deletion; ADB mode skips
  it honestly and kills com.google.android.gms.unstable (the DroidGuard process) instead.
- WalletRefreshResult gains three honest states: CACHE_CLEARED_ROOT (immediate recovery),
  PROCESSES_KILLED_ONLY (ADB — verdict expires on TTL ~1hr), FORCE_STOPPED_ONLY (no Shizuku).
- ServiceDoctorActivity shows the "Clear Play Services Data" button for non-root outcomes
  so users always have an immediate-recovery path.
- Rename button label "Cache" → "Data" since the action opens GMS storage settings for
  a full data clear, not just cache.

Add Play Integrity warmup to ADB-mode Wallet recovery

In ADB shell mode (uid 2000), the ~1hr Play Integrity verdict TTL was
the only barrier to immediate recovery after removing su bridge files.
This adds two best-effort mechanisms to shortcircuit it:

1. GSERVICES_OVERRIDE broadcast with candidate TTL key names set to 1ms,
   causing GMS to treat its verdict cache as immediately expired on next
   start. Key names are not published; unknown keys are silently ignored.

2. Play Integrity warmup call via IntegrityManagerFactory after GMS
   force-stops and restarts. If GMS re-runs DroidGuard on cold start
   (which it typically does), the fresh evaluation with clean binaries
   overwrites the old "compromised" verdict on disk before Wallet opens.

The warmup uses Tasks.await() with a 5s timeout from Dispatchers.IO.
A short delay(800) gives GMS time to restart after force-stop before
the warmup call is made. Both mechanisms fail gracefully — exceptions
are caught and logged; the pm clear Wallet + NFC re-assertion path
still runs regardless.

Also adds com.google.android.play:integrity:1.4.0 dependency to the
database module, ProGuard keep for Play Integrity classes, and updates
the ADB-mode success message to reflect the new recovery steps.
